{"metadata":{"description":"Authenticated remote access for a DeepSeek Harness web profile: TLS, QR/passcode device pairing, password sign-in, and per-device revocation in front of an untouched loopback harness.","id":"gh:1341351285","install_available":true,"language":"TypeScript","name":"deepseek-harness-relay","slug":"sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay","topics":["android","authentication","deepseek-harness","dsh-plugin","mdns","mobile","relay","reverse-proxy","self-hosted","tls"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Authenticated remote access for a DeepSeek Harness web profile: TLS, QR/passcode device pairing, pas"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"sword sign-in, and per-device revocation in front of an untouched loopback harness."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-relay"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"Use your DeepSeek Harness from your phone without opening it up to everyone on your Wi-Fi."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"dsh-relay is a plugin for the harness's web profile. It puts HTTPS, a password, and device pairing i"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"n front of the harness, so you can reach it from another device on your network, or from anywhere if"},{"id":"p4s3","text":" you forward a port."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"It's built on DeepSeek Harness, but it isn't an official DeepSeek project."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"The plugin installs straight from this repository, so the GitHub URL is all you need — no local chec"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"kout, and nothing to build by hand."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"**In the harness.** Open **Plugins** in the sidebar, choose **Add plugin**, paste this URL, and pres"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"ss.** Open **Plugins** in the sidebar, choose **Add plugin**, paste this URL, and press **Install**:"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"The first install fetches the plugin's sources and builds them in a temporary copy on your machine, "},{"id":"p10s2","text":"which takes a few seconds. pnpm refuses a git package's build script until you allow it, so the inst"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"aller asks; choose **Allow these scripts and retry**. When it finishes, choose **Enable now**, or sw"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"itch the bundle on in the list."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"**From a terminal.** The same URL works with the CLI, which forwards to pnpm inside the profile:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"For the desktop app, use **Plugins** inside the app, or target its profile:"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"If the terminal install stops with `allowBuilds`, copy the block pnpm printed into the profile's `pn"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"pm-workspace.yaml` and run the same command again. It looks like this:"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"The **Plugins** dialog writes that permission for you."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"The URL installs whatever is on `main`, which is the latest release. To pin a release or a commit, u"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"se pnpm's shorthand with a tag or SHA:"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"Prefer files that are already built? The npm package is the same code with `lib/` in it, and install"},{"id":"p20s2","text":"ing it runs no build script:"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"## Why this exists"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"The harness web app only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so only the computer running it can open it. That's"},{"id":"p23s2","text":" deliberate. The harness is a coding agent that runs commands on your machine, and its authors refus"},{"id":"p23s3","text":"e `dsh web --host 0.0.0.0` because it "would expose remote code execution to the network"."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"The common workaround is a config patch that binds the harness to `0.0.0.0` with no sign-in at all. "},{"id":"p24s2","text":"After that, anyone on the same Wi-Fi can drive your agent and run commands on your computer."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"dsh-relay is the safer way to do it. The harness stays on loopback, and the relay runs as a second l"},{"id":"p25s2","text":"istener next to it. Every request gets TLS and a credential check before the relay forwards it."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"Because the harness never leaves loopback, a relay that crashes or is misconfigured leaves the harne"},{"id":"p27s2","text":"ss unreachable from the network, never open to it. The relay also refuses to start if it finds the h"},{"id":"p27s3","text":"arness already listening on a network address."},{"id":"p28s1","text":"Harness 0.1.2 and later have a sign-in of their own (a browser session cookie). They still refuse to"},{"id":"p28s2","text":" bind to the network, still have no TLS, and only hand out that cookie on their own page, so a phone"},{"id":"p28s3","text":" still has no safe way in without something like this relay."},{"id":"p29s1","text":"## What you get"},{"id":"p30s1","text":"- Password sign-in from any browser. Too many wrong guesses lock that address out for a while.
- Pai"},{"id":"p30s2","text":"ring by QR code or an 8-digit code. Each paired device gets its own token, and you can revoke any de"},{"id":"p30s3","text":"vice on its own. Codes are single-use, expire after five minutes, and can only be created on the mac"},{"id":"p30s4","text":"hine running the harness.
- A "sign out everywhere" button that rotates the signing key and logs out"},{"id":"p30s5","text":" every browser and device at once.
- HTTPS, with your own certificate or a self-signed one whose key"},{"id":"p30s6","text":" apps can pin.
- mDNS advertisement on `_dsh._tcp`, so apps can find the relay without scanning your"},{"id":"p30s7","text":" subnet.
- The full harness web UI, unchanged, with a small **Relay** link in the corner when the pa"},{"id":"p30s8","text":"ge is served through the relay.
- A **Relay** action at the sidebar foot, one click from the account"},{"id":"p30s9","text":" menu, that changes the app to the relay's pairing, device, and password pages — in place, in the sa"},{"id":"p30s10","text":"me window.
- A **Computers** page that links this relay with another PC in either direction: share t"},{"id":"p30s11","text":"his PC, or connect to another one and open its harness in this browser with one click.
- A settings "},{"id":"p30s12","text":"page at **Plugins → dsh-relay → Configure** on the machine running the harness. Changes apply when y"},{"id":"p30s13","text":"ou press Save, with no restart."},{"id":"p31s1","text":"## Supported harness versions"},{"id":"p32s1","text":"| Harness | dsh-relay |"},{"id":"p33s1","text":"| 0.1.7-rc.2 through 0.2.x | **0.3** (tested on 0.2.1-rc.3, 0.2.0-rc.2, and 0.1.7-rc.2) |
| 0.1.2 th"},{"id":"p33s2","text":"rough 0.1.5 | 0.2, installed from its git tag: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:sorsama/deepseek"},{"id":"p33s3","text":"-harness-relay#v0.2.1`. The 0.2.1 package on npm shipped a stale build that can't authenticate to th"},{"id":"p33s4","text":"e harness. |
| 0.1.1 and earlier | 0.1 |"},{"id":"p34s1","text":"If you install a version that doesn't match your harness, the harness refuses to load it and tells y"},{"id":"p34s2","text":"ou which range it needs. 0.3 depends on the settings system added in harness 0.1.7, and 0.2 hangs th"},{"id":"p34s3","text":"e web app on 0.1.7 and later, so the two can't overlap."},{"id":"p35s1","text":"### The desktop app"},{"id":"p36s1","text":"The DeepSeek Harness desktop app runs the same web-app profile, so the relay works there too — it fr"},{"id":"p36s2","text":"onts the app's internal loopback server, and you don't need to run `dsh web` beside it. Install it f"},{"id":"p36s3","text":"rom inside the app: **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste the GitHub URL, press **Install**, then **Enable"},{"id":"p36s4","text":" now**, and restart the app to load it. `https://127.0.0.1:3443/relay/health` answers once the relay"},{"id":"p36s5","text":" is up. Do not add a redirect from the harness's own port to the relay's origin: the app's window ca"},{"id":"p36s6","text":"nnot complete a navigation to the relay's self-signed certificate, and that failure is fatal to the "},{"id":"p36s7","text":" complete a navigation to the relay's self-signed certificate, and that failure is fatal to the app."},{"id":"p37s1","text":"## Security"},{"id":"p38s1","text":"Signing in to the relay gives you the same power as a shell on the host machine, because the agent r"},{"id":"p38s2","text":"uns commands there. Everything in this plugin is designed around that fact. docs/SECURITY.md explain"},{"id":"p38s3","text":"s what the relay protects against, what it doesn't, and how to report a vulnerability."}],"truncated":true}
